column3: Set-Cookie values and the raw header text are discarded at the probe boundary: the synthetic GET response keeps only a value-free observation per cookie (a name label, flag presence, a classified SameSite and a Path=/ boolean), and its header map has no set-cookie key. Reason: a cookie value is a secret (safety model 3).
SameSite is a closed enum (lax, strict, none, other) and Path a boolean; no attribute value is retained. BootUI's checks read only those classifications. Reason: safety model 3.
A first segment with no = after its first character is shown as (unnamed); BootUI shows the whole segment, which can be the cookie value. Reason: safety model 3.

a cookie name that the secret-value detector matches, tested on the full name before the 80-character shortening, is shown as (redacted); the engine otherwise treats names as non-secret, so this is stricter than it. Severity logic sees an INFO label. Reason: fail closed.

Cookie names and the mount paths of the session checks pass through the masker one by one before the 240-character cut and read [masked] under METADATA_ONLY; classification runs on the unmasked label. Reason: safety model 3, consistent with pentesting:cors-evidence-masking.

a nameless padded base64 value (dGVzdA==; Secure) keeps its unpadded part as the label, as RFC 6265bis reads a name; it cannot be told from a name and is pinned by a test. Under FULL exposure a long name the secret detector does not match (for example several concatenated tokens) is shown as its first 80 characters.

PT-A02-008 evidence lists the recognised Cache-Control directive names (numeric arguments of at most ten digits for max-age, s-maxage and the stale-* directives only) and a count of the other directives, not the raw header text that BootUI joins. Reason: header values are never echoed (the A10 module invariant) and masking cannot keep the text readable.

the capture middleware of the host records the probe exchange like any exchange of the host. Under FULL its Set-Cookie value is shown, and under MASKED and FULL its Cache-Control value is recorded as sent because header masking decides by header name; MASKED and METADATA_ONLY records hold no cookie value. Pentesting evidence never echoes either header value. Reason: FULL is the opt-in to unmasked text, and changing header masking is a separate decision.

PT-A02-004 and PT-A02-006 read the SessionMiddleware keyword options (https_only passed as False, same_site none) from the static security facts instead of server.servlet.session.cookie.*; the target, evidence and recommendation name the middleware option, and the evidence names the echoed mount path of a mounted sub-application, never an option value. IDs, titles, severities, confidence and categories are BootUI's. Reason: the Spring properties do not exist.

facts that are absent or carry any limitation record BootUI's gap (Framework configuration evidence was incomplete.) and make the scan PARTIAL; the limitation text, which can carry a mount path, is never copied, and counting every limitation rather than only the session-related ones is the conservative default.
Starlette's session clear writes the value null with a 1970 expiry; BootUI's deletion rule needs a blank, empty-quoted or deleted value, so the cookie is evaluated like any other, as BootUI does.

The session configuration checks are not ported for Flask: app.config always holds SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE with defaults, so an explicit false cannot be told from the default, and the Flask adapter has no pentesting scan.
The Security panel rules SEC-SESSION-002 and SEC-SESSION-004 stay; the pentesting checks report separate evidence under their own IDs, as BootUI's two panels do.
